risk_if_not_implemented: Without USML or CCL Identification, the organization may fail to meet statutory, regulatory or contractual obligations, or be unable to demonstrate conformity when required. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Regulatory / Legal / Contractual Financial Liability (R-EX-5), Loss of Authorization / Certification / License (R-EX-11), Unaddressed Security / Compliance Exposure (R-GV-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11), Sanctions / Trade Restriction Disruption (MT-19).

compensating_control_1.name: Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI)
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to minimize risk associated with Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) through Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) practices.
compensating_control_1.justification: Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) (TPM-20) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of USML or CCL Identification (CPL-24.1) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Statutory, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the identification and implementation of relevant statutory, regulatory and contractual controls.
compensating_control_2.justification: Statutory, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance (CPL-02) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of USML or CCL Identification (CPL-24.1) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
